newsitem.title: USA: GM June U.S. sales fall 13 percent.
newsitem.headline: GM June U.S. sales fall 13 percent.

text.p: General Motors Corp. on Wednesday posted a 13.3 percent U.S. June sales decline, its biggest monthly sales slump since the beginning of 1997.

The U.S. No. 1 automaker said its passenger car sales tumbled 16.7 percent to 225,087. Total truck sales were 158,069, a drop of 7.8 percent. GM blamed the drops on an overall market slump and two costly work stoppages.

GM said Monday that a continuing strike at its Pontiac, Mich., full-size pickup truck plant and an earlier strike at its Malibu and Cutlass car plant in Oklahoma City resulted in the loss of 96,000 units in the second quarter.

On the car side, GM said all of its divisions except Cadillac reported lower sales in June. GM spokesman Dean Rotondo said newer car models, such as the Pontiac Grand Prix, which rose 140 percent to 11,492, continue to catch on with consumers. But he said those gains are offset by slower sales of older models.

GM's truck sales were hurt by the Pontiac, Mich., work stoppage. Sales of GM's popular Chevrolet C/K full-size pickup truck were down 15 percent to 37,104 units. Rotondo noted that sales of GM's new family of minivans were all up for the month.

Analysts had expected an overall drop of 11 percent to 16 percent for GM, the second member of the Detroit's Big Three to report U.S. June sales. Chrysler Corp. on Tuesday said sales fell 4 percent. Ford Motor Co. is scheduled to report Thursday.
